apiKeys.title: API Keys
apiKeys.description: Create API keys for programmatic access
apiKeys.name: Name

apiKeys.keyWarning: Make sure to copy this key now. You won't be able to see it again.
apiKeys.environmentsHint: Leave empty to allow every environment.
apiKeys.additionalPermissionsHint: Grant individual permissions on top of the selected roles. You can only grant what you hold yourself.
apiKeys.grantsRequired: Select at least one role or permission.
apiKeys.cannotGrant: You do not hold every permission in this role
apiKeys.noAccess: You need the api_keys.view or api_keys.manage permission to see API keys.
apiKeys.deleteKeyConfirm: Permanently delete this revoked API key? Its audit history stays; the key record and its grants are removed.

detail.notFoundDescription: This key no longer exists, or you do not have permission to view it.
detail.permissionsHint: Everything this key asks for, and whether the owner's own rights allow it to be used.
detail.matrixBlockedHint: The owner does not hold this permission, so the key cannot use it.
detail.matrixWildcardBody: This key carries the wildcard grant. It is allowed every permission its owner holds.

permissions.wildcardDescription: Grants unrestricted access to all resources and settings.
permissions.wildcardSummary: Wildcard grants unrestricted access. Stored as "*".
permissions.summary: {{grants}} granted, {{denies}} denied (deny is preview-only until the backend supports it).
permissions.containersManageSelfNote: On the environment McHarbor runs on this is admin-equivalent: it can start a container that mounts the Docker socket or the host. Acting on McHarbor's own containers also needs host_self.manage.

https.fingerprintHint: Compare this with the fingerprint your browser's certificate viewer shows. It is also printed in the server log at startup.

ca.title: Local root certificate authority
ca.description: Install this root once per machine and every browser on it trusts this host without warnings, including after the certificate is rotated.
ca.downloadError: Failed to download the root certificate
ca.missing: No local root certificate authority is available.
ca.installHint: macOS: add it to the System keychain and mark it Always Trust. Windows: import it into Trusted Root Certification Authorities. Linux: copy it into /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and run update-ca-certificates. Firefox keeps its own store and must be told separately.

pinning.title: Pin this certificate on remote agents
pinning.description: Every install method pins automatically while the agent dialog's self-signed switch is on: the one-line script, the Docker and Compose snippets, the binary and systemd unit, and the SSH deploy all set MCHARBOR_PIN to the root CA fingerprint above, so the agent trusts that one authority and nothing else. The root is pinned rather than the server certificate, so the pin survives the automatic 90-day renewal and a regenerate. Agents installed earlier keep MCHARBOR_INSECURE until you set the pin on them by hand.

https.title: HTTPS
https.description: Manage the TLS certificate and HTTPS enforcement for McHarbor.
https.subject: Subject:
https.enableHttpsDescription: Serve traffic over TLS using the uploaded certificate.
https.forceHttpsDescription: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS via X-Forwarded-Proto. For reverse proxy setups.
https.restartDescription: TLS changes take effect after container restart.
https.restartDescriptionNative: TLS changes take effect after McHarbor restarts (systemctl restart mcharbor).

warning.selfSigned: This host serves a certificate issued by its own local certificate authority. Download the root below and install it once per machine to remove browser warnings, or upload a publicly-trusted certificate instead.

regenerate.confirmBody: A new server certificate will be issued. The local root certificate authority is kept, so machines that already trust it stay trusted; any client pinning the old fingerprint needs the new one.

scanning.emptyDescription: Install a scanner plugin from the App Store to start scanning container images for vulnerabilities.
scanning.selectEngineDescription: Pick the engine this scanner will use. It cannot be changed later.
scanning.configurationDescription: Name this scanner and set how it should run.
scanning.name: Name
scanning.binaryMissingNativeHint: The plugin downloads {{engine}} into its own folder when it starts, and removes it with the plugin. Run Test to see why it is not there yet.

test.title: Test {{name}}

scanning.confirmDeleteDescription: Removes the configuration for {{name}}. The plugin stays installed and past scan results are kept.
scanning.autoScanDescription: Automatically scan container images for vulnerabilities during lifecycle events.
scanning.scanOnInstallDescription: Automatically scan images when installing apps from the App Store
scanning.scanOnUpdateDescription: Automatically scan images when updating installed apps

identity.issuerUrlDescription: Enter the OIDC issuer URL. McHarbor will discover the authorization, token, and userinfo endpoints automatically.

identity.fetchGroupsDescription: Fetch groups from the identity provider API to pre-populate mappings
identity.groupMappingDescription: Manually map specific provider groups to existing McHarbor groups
identity.groupMappingHint: When a user signs in via SSO, their provider group memberships are matched against these mappings and the corresponding McHarbor group memberships are applied.
identity.callbackUrlHint: Use this URL as the redirect URI in your provider configuration
identity.deleteProviderConfirm: Are you sure you want to delete this identity provider? Users who signed in through this provider will no longer be able to use SSO.
identity.noAdaptersInstalled: No identity provider plugins are installed.

scanHistory.title: Security scans
scanHistory.description: Inspect every container vulnerability scan across all environments and images.

autoLogout.title: Automatic sign-out
autoLogout.description: Sign users out after a period of inactivity. Only real input — typing, clicking, scrolling — counts as activity, so a dashboard left open in a forgotten tab does not keep the session alive.
autoLogout.enableHint: Turn this off to let sessions run to their 24-hour limit.
autoLogout.invalid: Enter a number between {{min}} and {{max}} seconds.

mfaRequirement.title: Require two-factor authentication
mfaRequirement.description: Decide who must sign in with a second factor. A user who is covered and has not enrolled yet is held on a setup screen after their password until they enrol; nothing else in McHarbor answers them until then.
mfaRequirement.hint: If this covers you and you have not enrolled, you will be asked to set it up straight after saving. API keys are not affected.

off.label: Optional
off.description: Everyone chooses for themselves in their profile.

all.label: Everyone
all.description: Required for every user, including single sign-on accounts.

resetTtl.title: Password reset link
resetTtl.description: Configure how long password-reset links remain valid.
resetTtl.label: Reset link lifetime

resetEmail.description: Choose which email channel carries password-reset links, and what the message says. Until a channel is picked, reset links are issued but never sent.
resetEmail.channelNone: Not configured — do not send email

resetEmail.noChannels: No email communication channel is configured yet. Add an SMTP, Gmail, or Exchange channel under Settings > Notifications > Channels, then come back to pick it here.
resetEmail.fromHint: Optional. Leave blank to use the sender already configured on the channel.
resetEmail.bodyHint: Plain text. The placeholders below are replaced when the email is sent, and the {{token}} placeholder is required.
resetEmail.invalidFrom: Enter a valid email address, or leave the field blank.
resetEmail.subjectRequired: Enter a subject for the reset email.
resetEmail.bodyRequired: Enter a message body for the reset email.
resetEmail.linkRequired: The message body must contain {{token}} — without it the recipient has no way to reset their password.

owner.description: Owners can manage the stack even without the global manage permission. Choose a user to assign ownership to, or clear the field to unassign.
owner.errorInvalidUser: That user does not exist or is disabled.

editor.name: Name

tester.description: Provide sample user, environment, and resource attributes to see whether this policy would match.

delete.title: Delete policy?

elevations.requestDescription: Ask for a permission for a limited time. An approver decides, and the grant lapses on its own when the window ends.
elevations.noneElevatable: No permission in the catalog is marked as requestable.
elevations.mineDescription: Requests you have made, and how they were decided.
elevations.noneMine: You have not requested elevated access.
elevations.inboxDescription: Requests waiting on a decision. Approving grants the permission until the window ends.
elevations.nonePending: Nothing is waiting for a decision.
elevations.policyDescription: Choose which permissions people may request. Operational permissions such as manage, delete, run and restore are requestable by default; permissions that administer access itself are not. Your choice overrides the default.

resetPassword.title: Reset password
resetPassword.description: Set a new password for this account, or force the user to choose one at next sign-in.
resetPassword.forceLabel: Force a reset at next sign-in
resetPassword.forceHint: The current password remains valid until the user signs in.

disableAccount.title: Disable account
disableAccount.description: Disable {{username}}'s account. All active sessions will be revoked immediately.

cli.title: Command-line client
cli.description: Download mcharbor for your platform and sign it in to this McHarbor with an API key.
cli.none: No client archives are available on this server.
cli.loadFailed: The client downloads could not be listed.
cli.loginHint: Unpack the archive, put mcharbor on your PATH, then run this and paste an API key when asked:

device.title: Approve a command-line sign-in
device.description: A terminal running mcharbor login --device is waiting. Enter the code it shows, then choose what its key may do.
device.onlyYours: Approve only a code you started yourself. The key is created for you and can be revoked under Security → API keys.
device.approved: Approved. The terminal receives its key within a few seconds and can be closed from here.
device.denied: Denied. The terminal has been told.
device.notFound: No waiting sign-in has that code. It may have expired (codes last 10 minutes) or already been decided.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.description: Destructive actions an approval rule holds until someone other than the requester approves them. The requester then runs the approved action once.
approvals.empty: No approval requests match this filter.
approvals.approveDescription: {{requester}} asks to {{category}} ({{resource}}). Approving lets them run it once, before the request expires.
approvals.denyDescription: {{requester}} asks to {{category}} ({{resource}}). Denying closes the request; it can never run.
approvals.notePlaceholder: Why you decided this way (recorded in the audit log)
approvals.executeDescription: This runs {{category}} on {{resource}} exactly as it was requested, as you, and only once. Your permissions are checked again now.
approvals.cancelDescription: The request closes and can no longer be approved or run.
approvals.resultFailed: The approved action ran and the server answered {{status}} ({{code}}).

rules.title: Approval rules
rules.description: Which destructive actions need a second person, how many approvers, who may approve, and how long a request stays open. With no rule, actions run immediately.
rules.empty: No rules yet. Every destructive action runs without approval.
rules.dialogDescription: A rule applies to every route of its category. An environment-specific rule wins over an all-environments rule.
rules.deleteDescription: {{category}} will run immediately again, without approval. Requests already held keep their terms.

simulator.title: Policy simulator
simulator.description: Ask whether a user may do something, and why: role grants, elevations, break-glass, overrides and ABAC policies, evaluated by the live authorization code.
simulator.anyOf: Any one of these permissions passes this gate.
simulator.ungated: This route has no permission gate.
simulator.exempt: This route is exempt from permission gates: {{reason}}
simulator.policyPathAllows: Routes that use owner rules and overrides would allow it.
simulator.policyPathDenies: Routes that use owner rules and overrides would deny it.

reasons.wildcard_role: Granted by the wildcard in role {{name}}
reasons.elevation: Granted by an approved, unexpired elevation
reasons.break_glass: Granted by an open break-glass session
reasons.no_grant: No role, elevation or policy grants it

conflicts.category_wildcard: Role {{name}} lists {{permissions}}; category wildcards are not expanded, so these grant nothing.
conflicts.policy_shadowed: Policy {{name}} never decides {{permissions}}: {{related}} always matches first.
conflicts.policy_tie: Policies {{related}} and {{name}} have the same priority and opposite effects on {{permissions}}; the name decides which runs first.

lifecycle.title: User lifecycle
lifecycle.description: Find disabled, locked, inactive or unprotected accounts and act on many at once. Every bulk action is previewed first.
lifecycle.previewDescription: This preview shows what will happen to each selected user. Nothing has changed yet.

breakGlass.selfDescription: A designated break-glass account can open time-limited full access in an emergency. Using it pages every account manager and writes an error-level audit entry.
breakGlass.notDesignated: Your account is not designated for break-glass access.
breakGlass.activateDescription: You get every permission for up to {{max}} minutes. The reason is sent to every account manager and kept in the audit log.
breakGlass.reasonPlaceholder: What is broken and why normal access is not enough (at least 10 characters)
breakGlass.passwordHint: Opening emergency access needs you to prove it is you, even in an active session.
breakGlass.adminDescription: Accounts allowed to open emergency access, and every time they did.
breakGlass.undesignateDescription: {{user}} can no longer open emergency access, and any open session ends.
breakGlass.noHistory: Break-glass access has never been used.

apiKeys.rotateDescription: {{name}} gets a new secret with the same grants and lifetime. The current secret stops working at once; the new one is shown only once.
